items.caption:
Broken sleep may dent positive mood more than a late bedtime.
In a 2015 lab study of 62 healthy adults, 3 nights of forced awakenings lowered positive mood more than a later bedtime, with a similar loss of total sleep. A lab finding, not advice.

items.caption:
After a short night, good moments may lift you less.
In a daily-diary study of 1,982 US adults (published 2020), sleeping less than usual the night before was linked to a smaller boost in positive emotion from positive events. An association, not advice.

items.caption:
POV: the day after a sleepless night.
In one 2007 brain-scan experiment with healthy young adults, staying awake about 35 hours left the amygdala (the brain's alarm centre) about 60% more reactive to upsetting pictures than after a normal night, with a weaker link to the front of the brain. A 2020 study linked more deep sleep to lower anxiety the next day. Small studies of healthy adults, and the deep-sleep result is a link, not proof. If it keeps costing you sleep, talk to a doctor.
